{{Short description|Subring consisting of the elements x}}
{{Use American English|date=March 2021}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2021}}

In [[Abstract algebra|algebra]], the '''center of a ring''' {{mvar|R}} is the [[subring]] consisting of the elements {{mvar|x}} such that {{nowrap|{{math|1=''xy'' = ''yx''}}}} for all elements {{mvar|y}} in {{mvar|R}}. It is a [[commutative ring]] and is denoted as {{math|Z(''R'')}}; 'Z' stands for the German word {{lang|de|Zentrum}}, meaning "center".

If {{mvar|R}} is a ring, then {{mvar|R}} is an [[associative algebra]] over its center. Conversely, if {{mvar|R}} is an associative algebra over a commutative subring {{mvar|S}}, then {{mvar|S}} is a subring of the center of {{mvar|R}}, and if {{mvar|S}} happens to be the center of {{mvar|R}}, then the algebra {{mvar|R}} is called a '''central algebra'''.

== Examples ==
* The center of a commutative ring {{mvar|R}} is {{mvar|R}} itself.
* The center of a [[skew-field]] is a [[field (mathematics)|field]].
* The center of the (full) [[matrix ring]] with entries in a commutative ring {{mvar|R}} consists of {{mvar|R}}-scalar multiples of the [[identity matrix]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://math.stackexchange.com/q/27808 |title=vector spaces – A linear operator commuting with all such operators is a scalar multiple of the identity |website=Math.stackexchange.com |date= |accessdate=2017-07-22}}</ref>
* Let {{mvar|F}} be a [[field extension]] of a field {{mvar|k}}, and {{mvar|R}} an algebra over {{mvar|k}}. Then <math>\operatorname{Z}(R \otimes_k F) = \operatorname{Z}(R) \otimes_k F</math>.
* The center of the [[universal enveloping algebra]] of a [[Lie algebra]] plays an important role in the [[representation theory of Lie algebras]]. For example, a [[Casimir element]] is an element of such a center that is used to analyze [[Lie algebra representation]]s. See also: ''[[Harish-Chandra isomorphism]]''.
* The center of a [[simple algebra]] is a field.
